name: Meridian Audio Concepts SirenSphere S-7 'Dome'
description:
A throwable sonic deterrent that creates a spherical zone of intolerable sound when deployed. The S-7 is a 6-centimeter rubberized sphere containing a multi-directional speaker array powered by a high-density capacitor. When armed and thrown, impact sensors activate the device on landing, generating a 155-decibel omni-directional sonic field within a three-meter radius. The sound profile cycles through twelve frequencies specifically selected to cause maximum discomfort across different hearing ranges, including frequencies that resonate painfully with common cochlear implant models.

Meridian Audio Concepts developed the S-7 as a 'drop and run' deterrent — the user throws the device at or near the threat, and the resulting wall of sound creates an impassable zone of pain while the user escapes in the opposite direction. The sphere operates for forty-five seconds before the capacitor depletes, after which the device is inert and non-recoverable. At Φ85 per unit, the S-7 is a single-use investment, but repeat customers are common enough that Meridian sells them in packs of three.

The S-7's impact on augmented individuals with cochlear implants or audio-processing cyberware is disproportionately severe — the resonance frequencies can cause feedback loops in audio hardware that result in incapacitating pain well beyond the physical sound's effect. This has led to complaints from augmented communities that the S-7 is discriminatory in its design.
specifications:
output: 155 dB within 3 meter radius
frequency cycling: 12 targeted frequencies
activation: impact sensor on landing
duration: 45 seconds
weight: 95 g
diameter: 6 cm
cost: Φ85 (single), Φ220 (3-pack)
reusable: no — single deployment
tactical_use: Arm by twisting the top hemisphere 90 degrees, then throw at the ground near the threat. The impact sensor triggers on any surface contact greater than 2G, so a firm toss to the ground is sufficient. Move away from the device before activation — the 155 dB output is harmful to the user within three meters. The S-7 is particularly effective in enclosed spaces where the sound reflects and amplifies. In open spaces, the effective radius may be slightly reduced.
cultural_context: The S-7 has found a niche as the preferred deterrent for people who don't trust their aim with sprays or their nerve with direct confrontation. Throwing something is intuitive and doesn't require pointing at an attacker. Meridian Audio Concepts leans into this psychology with marketing that shows ordinary people — commuters, parents, night-shift workers — deploying the S-7 without breaking stride. The product's augmentation-resonance issue has made it controversial, with some arguing it's a feature and others calling it a design flaw that disproportionately harms the aug-dependent.
story_hooks: A street gang has weaponized the S-7 by deploying dozens simultaneously in enclosed transit stations — the overlapping sonic fields create conditions so severe that even filtered security forces cannot enter, allowing the gang to operate freely for the forty-five-second window.

Meridian Audio Concepts is under investigation after a deaf individual with cochlear implants suffered permanent implant damage from an S-7 deployed by a panicking bystander — the device's aug-resonance feature is being called an accessibility rights violation.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, perfectly spherical self-defense device with a soft, approachable appearance that belies its acoustic lethality. The rounded form resembles a high-tech stress ball or training sphere, making it unassuming enough to carry in a pocket or palm. The top hemisphere features a subtle twist-lock mechanism that's barely visible when armed.
physical_description.dimensions: 6 cm diameter sphere; compact enough to fit in a closed fist
physical_description.weight_description: Light and balanced — 95 grams feels almost negligible in hand, lending itself to easy throwing and concealment. The weight distribution is perfectly neutral, centering in the palm without tilting.
physical_description.primary_material: Rubberized polymer composite with internal speaker array matrix and high-density capacitor core
physical_description.finish: Matte rubberized exterior with a subtle non-slip coating; the twist-lock seam on the top hemisphere is barely perceptible, finished flush with the sphere's surface
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with thin accent lines of electric blue running along the seam line where the hemispheres meet; subtle Meridian Audio Concepts branding in silver
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized, slightly tacky polymer surface designed for secure grip even with sweaty or augmented hands; micro-textured to prevent slipping during the throwing motion
distinctive_features: Minimal twist-lock mechanism at the top (90-degree rotation to arm) — almost invisible when not engaged
Faint circular perforations forming a grid pattern across the surface, concealing the multi-directional speaker array
Electric blue accent seam separating the two hemispheres
Small silver serial number stamp on the lower hemisphere
Impact-sensing nodules barely visible as slight dimples at cardinal points
No external indicators or LEDs — silent and dark until deployment
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Meridian Audio Concepts logo and 'SirenSphere S-7' embossed in silver on the upper hemisphere; serial number stamped in micro-font on the lower hemisphere; Φ85 cost marking visible on the glossy interior of the packing sleeve
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-pristine and inert until armed; once deployed, the sphere becomes a scorched, acoustically-dead husk — the capacitor burns out completely, leaving the device non-recoverable and technically trash. Customers typically see only pre-deployment units.
